question.problem: Let $\mathcal{B}= \left\{ \mathbf{b}_1, \mathbf{b}_2 \right\}$ be a basis of $\mathbb{R}^2$ and ![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14274943/assets/e8c67f642148caf84c01b7ee88fe125c4a5ae37ecae313d01d45c277de51d74b.svg) What are the coordinates of $\mathbf{x}$ relative to the basis $\mathcal{C}= \left\{ \mathbf{c}_1, \mathbf{c}_2 \right\},$ where $\mathbf{c}_1 = \mathbf{b}_2-\mathbf{b}_1$ and $\mathbf{c}_2 = 2\mathbf{b}_1 - 3\mathbf{b}_2?$
question.worked_solution:
We are given that

$$
\{\begin{aligned}{c}_{1}={b}_{2}-{b}_{1} \\ {c}_{2}=2{b}_{1}-3{b}_{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

First, we express the $\mathbf{b}$'s in terms of $\mathbf{c}$'s. Multiplying the first equation by $2$ and adding the equations, we get 

$$
2\mathbf{c}_1+\mathbf{c}_2 = -\mathbf{b}_2
\qquad\Longrightarrow\qquad
\mathbf{b}_2 = -2\mathbf{c}_1-\mathbf{c}_2.
$$

Substituting this into the first equation, we obtain

$$
\mathbf{c}_1 = \left( -2\mathbf{c}_1-\mathbf{c}_2 \right) - \mathbf{b}_1
\qquad\Longrightarrow\qquad
\mathbf{b}_1 = -3\mathbf{c}_1-\mathbf{c}_2.
$$

Since ![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14274943/assets/0e283c9948eacf3e231eef3a3feb355c33f20c3dbfd89e97c530331758af34ad.svg) we can write the vector $\mathbf{x}$ in terms of the vectors $\mathbf c_1$ and $\mathbf c_2,$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}x & ={b}_{1}-3{b}_{2} \\  & =(-3{c}_{1}-{c}_{2})-3(-2{c}_{1}-{c}_{2}) \\  & =-3{c}_{1}-{c}_{2}+6{c}_{1}+3{c}_{2} \\  & =3{c}_{1}+2{c}_{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, ![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14274943/assets/d8d25ca46df4435c67e7c23e61851e2acd4826b0b2d99d9b54de8b6f2c37ee94.svg)
